verdict.rationale: Better Stack documents background automations that run on their own. Monitors check URLs every X seconds and automatically create incidents and alert on-call. Escalation policies escalate unacknowledged incidents without anyone stepping in. Incident triggers can post todo lists and route incidents, and exceptions produce suggested-fix pull requests. However, the AI SRE explicitly never takes automated actions without approval, and there is no evidence of a general user-defined automation or workflow builder. missing for 10: general-purpose user-configurable automation/workflow builder, autonomous AI agent actions without approval, depth of documentation on triggered incident workflows, independent corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: An HTTP status code monitor checks your URLs every X seconds for an HTTP success status code (2XX). If the URL doesn't return this code, the monitor creates an Incident and alerts the current on-call person.
Post a todo list when a new incident is triggered. Route the incident to the right responder.
If they don’t acknowledge the incident (for example, after 3 minutes), it escalates and notifies everyone on the team.
Got an exception? Get a pull request with a suggested fix waiting for you in GitHub.
Get an automated post-mortem based on the incident timeline and Slack.
